title: Questions to Ask During an Initial Architect Consultation in Scarsdale
excerpt: Before you hire an architect for your Scarsdale home project, know which questions matter most. Here's what to cover in your first meeting.
content:
You've decided to renovate your Scarsdale home. Now comes the part that makes many homeowners nervous: the initial consultation with an architect. What do you even ask? How do you know if this person is right for your project?

The good news is that a solid first conversation doesn't require you to be an expert. You just need to ask the right questions. This will help you understand how an architect thinks, how they work, and whether they're the right fit for what you're building or remodeling.

Verify Their Credentials and Experience

Start by asking whether the architect is licensed by New York State. This matters. A licensed architect in New York has met education, experience, and exam requirements that protect you as a homeowner. Not all designers carry this credential, and that's an important distinction.

You should also ask about their experience with projects like yours. Are they comfortable with kitchen remodels? Have they done primary suite additions? Historic restorations? Home additions in Westchester require an understanding of local codes, lot constraints, and what works in neighborhoods like Scarsdale.

One more thing to ask: do they also hold a general contractor license? Some architects do, some don't. If they're a general contractor in Westchester as well, that means they understand construction from both sides. They know what works on paper and what actually works on site.

Understand Their Design-Build Approach

Ask how they typically work with clients. Do they hand off designs and disappear, or do they stay involved through construction? A design-build approach in Westchester means one person or firm handles both the design and the construction. This is different from traditional architecture, where the architect designs and a separate contractor builds.

In a design-build model, the architect has skin in the game. They're accountable for what they design because they're the ones building it. That matters for quality and problem-solving.

Ask About the Process and Timeline

Find out what their typical process looks like from start to finish. How many design phases do they build in? When do permits happen? When does construction start? What happens if code issues come up during permitting?

Ask specifically about Scarsdale's permit process. Every Westchester municipality has its own building department and review timeline. Scarsdale is no different. A residential architect in Scarsdale should be familiar with how this town's inspectors work and what they look for. That experience saves time and headaches.

Also ask about budget. How do they manage costs? Do they help you understand where your money goes? Are there phases where you can stop and reassess before moving forward?

Get a Sense of How They Communicate

Pay attention to how they answer your questions right now. Are they listening, or are they talking at you? Do they ask questions back about what you actually want? A good architect asks about your lifestyle, your priorities, and how you use your home.

Ask how often you'll hear from them during the project. Will they send regular updates? Can you reach them if something comes up? How do they handle decisions that need to be made quickly?

Your first consultation sets the tone for the entire relationship. If something feels off in that meeting, trust that instinct. You're about to spend months (or longer) working together, often making big financial and personal decisions about your home.
